newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua postpones sale of phone company stake.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua postpones sale of phone company stake.

text.p: Nicaragua has postponed the sale of a 40 percent stake in state telephone company Empresa Nicaraguense de Telecomunicaciones (Enitel) until next March, officials said on Thursday.

The Telecommunications Privatization Committee, made up of government representatives, an Enitel official and a labor representative, said in a statement the bidding processs for Enitel, originally slated for Thursday, had been put off.

"In the interests of the nation and the country's political and economic stability, we have postponed the public reception of bids for 40 percent of the shares of Enitel until March 31, 1997," the statement said.
The committee said various bidders had asked for a postponement because of the proximity of Nicaragua's October 20 presidential elections.
The election pits Arnoldo Aleman of the right-wing Liberal Alliance against former President Daniel Ortega of the left-wing Sandinista Front. The race is very close.

It is the second time the Enitel sale has been canceled at the last minute. The sale was originally set for July 27 but was canceled on the grounds that various bidders had asked for more time to study the company.
Even before that, the sale of Enitel was delayed for 18 months while Nicaragua's National Assembly debated the legislation governing the sale.
Enitel President Rolando Rivas said the delays have hurt, since 29 countries are now in the process of privatizing their telephone companies, making it a buyer's market.
The head of Nicaragua's Cabinet, Julio Cardenas, said the government expects to receive $120 million for the sale of 40 percent of Enitel's shares.
Spain's Telefonica Internacional is considered the favorite to buy Enitel, he said.
Enitel has said other qualified bidders include AT&T Corp, Korea Telecom, Sprint Corp, GTE Corp, STET International of Italy, France Telecom, and CTT of Chile.
